newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen trending up, extending rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa seen trending up, extending rally.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE cocoa futures are likely to motor higher on Monday, extending's last week rally with September eyeing the ultimate goal at 1,300 stg a tonne, technical analysts said.
Traders called the market to open 10 stg higher.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said cocoa appeared to be overbought but added this was not overly important.
The 14-day relative strength indicator stood at 77 percent, well in the overbought zone of 70-value barrier.
She said September was heading for the 1,142 stg mark, the high not seen since June last year based on the second-month continuation chart.
A break above 1,142 could take the market to the next upside target at 1,165.
"Further out, the ultimate goal is 1,300," she added.
On Friday September peaked at 1,134, the highest since June 19, 1996 and a fresh contract high, before slipping back on profit-taking and light origin sales in forward months.

The rally extended Thursday's surge on concerns the developing El Nino weather pattern would spark droughts in major cocoa-producing countries and disrupt next year's cocoa crop. There was also talk that early Ivory Coast settings for the new crop remained low.

Some traders were sceptical of the fundamental change said to be pushing cocoa prices higher, but said they could not ignore the strong uptrend developing on near- and intermediate-term technical charts.
Broker GNI said there was no specific reason to buy cocoa, but added, "The logic says if Ivorian production has stabilised, then the world will suffer a large supply deficit in the near future."
In the short term the market looked a bit heady, but any setback would be bought, the brokerage said in a daily commentary. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
